stages.name: Poverty and inequality
stages.title: Poverty and inequality
stages.sub: Tell apart a fixed poverty line from one that moves with everyone else's income.

steps.q: A family cannot afford enough food, warm clothing or a place to live. Are they able to meet a basic standard of living?
steps.right: No, they fall short of it
steps.wrong: Yes, as long as they have some income
steps.hint: Think about what having 'some money' actually buys them here.

steps.q: A country sets a fixed list of basics: enough food, water, shelter and clothing to survive. A family cannot afford this list even after ten years, even though prices and wages elsewhere have changed. What has stayed the same?
steps.wrong: The average income in that country
steps.hint: The list of basics does not move even if the rest of the economy does.

steps.q: A family can afford food, heating and shelter, but their income is far below what most other households in their country earn. If average incomes doubled next year, would the amount this family needs to avoid this kind of poverty change too?
steps.right: Yes, the benchmark would move with it
steps.hint: Is this family being compared to a fixed list, or to everyone else around them?

steps.q: Average incomes in a country rise sharply over 20 years, so the fixed list of basics becomes easy for almost everyone to afford. Could someone stop falling short of that fixed list, yet still earn far less than everyone else around them?
steps.right: Yes, the two benchmarks can move apart
steps.wrong: No, the two benchmarks always match
steps.hint: One measure never changes its target, the other resets every time the average changes.
